html:
An earthquake on 22 December 856 in the province of Qumis in northern Iran, then part of the Abbasid Caliphate. It wrecked the city of Damghan and is said to have killed about 200,000 people, which would place it among the deadliest earthquakes on record.

The quake struck along the southern edge of the Alborz mountains, on the main road between Iraq and Khorasan. Modern estimates give it a magnitude of about 7.9. Chroniclers report that much of Damghan was destroyed, along with many villages and towns in the region.

The death toll comes from medieval sources and cannot be checked, but the size of the damage zone shows it was a great quake. Iran sits where plates collide, and big earthquakes have struck its towns again and again, as did the 1138 Aleppo earthquake further west.
